index.title: Guides
index.heading: Obelisk Guides
index.subtitle: Everything about Obelisk: what it is, how it works, and where it's going. Written plain, no jargon walls.

alt.relayInstall: Two commands are the whole install: ./setup.sh gives you a relay on localhost, ./expose.sh gives the world a way in, no SSH session and no YAML to hand-edit.
alt.relayLadder: Admission is a ladder, not a switch: Tier 1 is added by hand, Tier 2 is two hops away in the follow graph, Tier 3 is three hops, and a block list overrides all three.
alt.relayNumbers: The reach of a single reference account on the public Obelisk relay: 166,735 keys admitted in total, split across Tier 1 at 1,062, Tier 2 at 45,966 and Tier 3 at 119,708 or more.
alt.relaySnapshot: A reported message still readable in the moderation queue after the author deleted it, because the relay captured its own copy when the report arrived.

alt.chainReactionBoard: Chain Reaction board in Obelisk: a 6×9 grid of dark cells holding glowing red, lime and cyan orbs, with a legend naming the three players and whose turn it is.
alt.chainReactionResult: Chain Reaction final standings in Obelisk: first place with a trophy and an orb count, second place marked out, under the heading "Final result".
alt.vestaBoard: Vesta board in Obelisk: a hexagonal island of resource tiles with numbered dice tokens, player settlements and roads on the edges, a robber on the desert, and each player’s hand and victory points below.
alt.stackerWell: A Stacker playfield in Obelisk: a ten-column well part-filled with coloured tetromino blocks and the ghost outline of the falling piece near the top.
alt.stackerTable: A live three-player Stacker match in Obelisk: the player’s own well with grey garbage lines at the bottom, hold and next-piece rails, and two opponents shown as miniature boards with their attack and line counts.
alt.gamePicker: The Obelisk "Pick a game" dialog listing Chain Reaction, Vesta and Stacker, each with a thumbnail, a one-line description, its player range and its turn clock.
alt.relayLanding: The connect card on an Obelisk Relay landing page: counters reading 28 groups and 9 supported NIPs, above the relay address wss://public.obelisk.ar with a copy button.
alt.relaySignIn: The Obelisk Relay admin sign-in card offering three Nostr identities: a NIP-07 browser extension, a NIP-46 remote signer, or a pasted private key marked risky in browsers.
alt.relayOverview: The Overview screen of the Obelisk Relay console: hourly graphs of active connections and disk used, live counters for connections, uptime and last event received, and a configured summary showing retention, database size and the access mode.
alt.relayAccessTabs: The Access screen of the Obelisk Relay console: a box for checking whether an account is allowed, five tabs counting Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3, Blocked and Policies, and the reference accounts every tier is measured from.
alt.relayBudgetLadder: The rate budget in the Obelisk Relay console: bars showing what each tier may publish: 6,000 events a minute for Tier 1, 3,000 for Tier 2, 1,500 for Tier 3 and 600 for no tier at all.
alt.relayKeySearch: Checking one account in the Obelisk Relay console: a pasted npub answered with "Allowed", admitted by web of trust at two hops from a reference account, with a Block button beside the verdict.
alt.relayReports: The Reports screen of the Obelisk Relay console: moderation reports grouped one row per reported thing, each tagged nudity or spam with its reporter count, a note field, and buttons to dismiss or block the reported account.
alt.relayStorage: The Storage screen of the Obelisk Relay console: 227.1 MB on disk holding 12,831 events, nothing deleted, with a warning that pruning stops the database file growing but does not shrink it.

alt.whatIsObelisk: Obelisk overview: an obelisk monument surrounded by orbiting Nostr keys and floating chat bubbles, illustrating a Discord-like group chat where identity is a Nostr keypair.
alt.howObeliskWorks: How Obelisk works: the Obelisk web app in your browser signs events with your key (kept by an extension, a signer app or an encrypted session on the device) and sends them straight to your server, a NIP-29 relay drawn as the Obelisco that stores and enforces channels, messages and roles. The app reaches other Nostr relays itself for profiles and DMs; voice goes peer to peer or through an SFU, and zaps are paid from a Lightning wallet.
alt.wot: Nostr Web of Trust graph for spam protection: your pubkey at the center, lime-green high-trust nodes connected through your follows, and red-outlined spam nodes pushed to the periphery.
alt.futureRelays: The future of Nostr: a mesh of relay-based groups exchanging encrypted NIP-29 messages with no central server, every relay equal.
alt.bitcoinZaps: Bitcoin Lightning zaps in chat: a chat message with a glowing lightning bolt flowing into it, orbited by satoshi particles, representing a zap sent over Nostr Wallet Connect (NIP-47).
alt.adminCli: Obelisk's in-app admin tools: the relay operator's server settings (profile, emoji, channels, roles, members) and a channel admin's settings (access, type, members), both publishing signed events to a NIP-29 relay that enforces them.
alt.swapAnything: The Obelisk ecosystem: one self-hostable Nostr relay connected to a chat client, a voice SFU, and a bot runtime: every component independently replaceable, nothing locked together.
alt.obeliskBots: Obelisk zap bot hero: a stylish robot with black sunglasses listening for Nostr zap receipts and group reactions, then posting signed kind 9 announcements into NIP-29 groups.
alt.quantumSafe: Quantum-safe DMs hero: a sealed message at the center wrapped in two shells, an inner classic secp256k1 key exchange and an outer post-quantum layer, illustrating hybrid protection.
alt.chainReaction: Chain Reaction hero: a dark grid of cells holding red, lime and cyan orbs with one cell bursting and pushing an orb into each of its four neighbours, the cascade played over a Nostr relay.
alt.vesta: Vesta hero: a hexagonal island of forest, brick, wool, grain and ore tiles with numbered dice tokens and player settlements, beside the event-log entropy the dice roll is derived from.
alt.stacker: Stacker hero: two ten-column wells of falling coloured blocks, a cleared line in the left well sending grey garbage rows into the right one over a Nostr relay.
alt.runYourOwnRelay: Admission to a self-hosted Nostr relay drawn as a ladder: the relay at the left, three widening arcs of admitted keys around it, added by hand, two hops away, three hops away, publishing at 6,000, 3,000 and 1,500 events a minute, and a block list that is checked first and overrides every tier.
alt.wotGraph: Web of Trust score computation: how Obelisk derives a trust score for a Nostr pubkey by walking the follow graph from your own follows outward.
alt.relayGroups: NIP-29 relay-based group: the relay holds the membership list (kind 39002), admin list (kind 39001), and message events (kind 9), and the client subscribes by group id.
alt.zapFlow: A NIP-57 zap in Obelisk: your client signs a zap request, the recipient's LNURL server returns a Lightning invoice, your wallet pays it over WebLN or NWC, and the LNURL server publishes the kind 9735 receipt to the relays for every client to show. No Obelisk server in the money path.
alt.swapMatrix: Obelisk swap matrix: every layer of the stack - client, voice, bots, relay - has independent alternatives, so any one component can be replaced without changing the others.
alt.markDex: obelisk-dex logo mark: a chat bubble containing the Obelisk monument, representing the browser chat client that signs Nostr events and posts them to a relay.
alt.markSfu: obelisk-sfu logo mark: a central voice mixer hub connected by spokes to five peers, representing the Selective Forwarding Unit that mixes streams for large group calls.
alt.markBots: obelisk-bots logo mark: a small robot head with an antenna, representing the bot runtime where each bot has its own Nostr keypair and posts messages like any user.
alt.markRelay: obelisk-relay logo mark: a relay tower broadcasting concentric signal arcs, representing the self-hostable Nostr relay with built-in whitelisting and admin UI.

whatIsObelisk.title: What is Obelisk
whatIsObelisk.desc: An obelisk monument surrounded by orbiting Nostr keys and floating chat bubbles.

howObeliskWorks.title: How Obelisk works
howObeliskWorks.desc: The Obelisk web app runs in your browser and signs every event with your key, which stays with you. It talks straight to your server, a NIP-29 relay that stores the channels, messages and roles and enforces them, and reaches other Nostr relays itself for profiles and DMs. Voice goes peer to peer or through an SFU, and zaps are paid from your Lightning wallet. There is no Obelisk server in between.
howObeliskWorks.serverDoes: stores the group and enforces its rules
howObeliskWorks.voiceSfu: or an SFU the admin picks

stacker.title: Two Stacker wells trading garbage lines
